The Envelope Under the Floorboard

地板下面的信封 · 600 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1Bea was preparing for her departure from a spacious cottage. The roof had deteriorated, and she could no longer carry a basket of laundry upstairs. Her grandson, Eli, wanted to renovate the house and rent it out. A vacant residence would cost more than it earned. Bea asked him to look in the downstairs room before he called an agent. She had left an envelope there when he was a child.

2Dust covered a mat beside the sewing table. Eli lifted a loose board and found a bundle of cotton tied with string. Inside were an envelope and a small tin token. A former tenant had left them after an intimate farewell dinner. His letter said Bea had helped him mend clothes and find work when his family had nowhere to reside. He left the token as a small sign of sincere gratitude.

3Eli had assumed the family was well-off. Their son had worn a fine sweater and carried a leather trunk. Bea said a neighbor who liked to knit had made the sweater. The trunk held all the family's possessions. The appearance of luxury had made their hardship invisible. Eli asked why they had settled in a narrow alley when a larger house stood across the square.

4The family needed accommodation near a workshop. It had no money for a deposit. Bea had agreed to a flexible lease and let the father pay in installments. An acquaintance helped furnish the cottage and carry in their baggage. The letter said that this help had kept the children in school until the father could earn a decent wage. Eli began to appreciate why his grandmother had kept such a humble token.

5An agent proposed a luxurious holiday home. Eli compared the cost with the likely revenue. A large mortgage would leave little money for repairs. A tenant from the clinic wanted a dry room and a neat kitchen. She already had a microwave and a small refrigerator. Bea asked the agent to arrange a visit. Eli patched a crack in the ceiling and used a mop to tidy the room.

6The visitor brought her twin brother, who made furniture in a garage. He offered to restore the table if he could use it after work. Eli had thought it was a nuisance. The brother brushed the dirt off an old repair and showed him how it had kept the wood from decay. Bea told them what she had kept in its drawer. For the first time, she could describe leaving the cottage without sounding sorrowful.

7The agent said a landlord had to provide a safe stair and adequate light. Eli accepted the obligation and arranged the work. The tenant asked if he could keep the shaded corner as it was. Her brother could sew there at midday in his leisure time. Eli had been looking for things to remove. Now he asked which parts still had a use. Eli admitted in a casual conversation that he had resented the cost of keeping the cottage. Bea acknowledged his concern. She regretted leaving him with the expense. Her first question, though, was whether they could accommodate a family without making them feel that they owed her anything.

8On moving day the old tenant returned with his daughter. Bea handed the envelope to Eli and kept the token. The daughter whispered that she hoped to hold her wedding reception there in spring. Eli put the date on the calendar and asked them to leave the table where it was. He could inherit a property and honor the people who had made a home there.

四级核心词汇 · 13中文译文

地板下面的信封

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1贝娅正准备离开自己那座宽敞的小屋。屋顶已经老化，她也没办法再提着一篮衣物上楼。孙子伊莱想翻修房子，再租出去。房子空着，花的钱会比赚的多。贝娅请他找房屋中介之前先看看楼下的屋子。伊莱还是孩子时，她在那里留过一个信封。

2缝纫桌旁有块垫子，已经落满了灰。伊莱掀起一块松动的地板，找到一包用细绳绑着的棉布。里面有一封信，还有一个小小的锡制纪念物。以前的租客吃完一顿亲友间的告别饭后，把它们留了下来。信上说，一家人曾经没地方住，是贝娅帮他补衣服、找工作。留下那件小东西，是为了真诚地道一声谢。

3伊莱一直以为那家人挺富裕。他们的儿子穿着好看的毛衣，提着一只皮箱。贝娅说，毛衣是一位爱织东西的邻居做的。皮箱里装的，是他们全家的家当。看起来有些体面的东西，把他们的难处遮住了。伊莱问，广场对面就有更大的房子，他们为什么要住到窄巷里？

4那一家需要在工坊附近有个住处，却拿不出押金。贝娅同意用灵活的租约，让父亲分期付租金。一个熟人帮着置办家具，还替他们把行李搬进去。信上说，多亏这些帮助，父亲拿到一份体面的工资之前，孩子们仍能继续上学。伊莱开始懂得，为什么祖母留着这么不起眼的纪念物。

5中介建议把小屋改成豪华度假屋。伊莱把改造成本和可能的收入对比了一下。背上大笔房贷，维修就剩不下多少钱。一个在诊所工作的租客只需要干燥的屋子和整洁的厨房。她已经有微波炉和小冰箱。贝娅让中介约个时间带她来看。伊莱补了天花板上的一道裂缝，再用拖把把房间收拾干净。

6来看房的人带来她的双胞胎哥哥。他在车库里做家具，愿意修好那张桌子，只问下班后能不能用。伊莱原先嫌那张桌子碍事。哥哥刷去一处旧修补上的泥，指给他看，这么补为什么能让木头不再烂下去。贝娅说起自己以前在抽屉里放了什么。这是她第一次谈到要搬走时，语气里没有难过。

7中介说，房东要提供安全的楼梯和足够的照明。伊莱接受了这份责任，安排人来修。租客问，能不能把有阴凉的那个角落留着。她哥哥中午有空时可以在那儿做针线活。伊莱原先到处找什么东西该扔，现在却问，还有什么用得上。闲聊时，他承认自己曾为留下小屋的费用感到不满。贝娅理解他的担心，也后悔让他承担这笔开销。她先想的，还是能不能让一家人有个住处，又不会觉得欠她人情。

8搬家那天，老租客带女儿回来了。贝娅把信封交给伊莱，自己留着纪念物。女儿小声说，希望春天能在这里办结婚宴。伊莱把日期记在日历上，又请大家把桌子留在原处。他可以继承一座房子，也可以记住曾在这里安家的人。
